title: Surjective enumeration characterization omits the empty-set exception.
details: Avigad, Computability and Incompleteness, version 2007-01-09, §1.3 printed p. 10 (PDF14), example 4 after Definition 1.3.3. Visually checked against the PDF. The claimed equivalence between countability of A and a surjection N→A fails for A=empty: the empty set is finite and hence countable, but a function from the nonempty N to it cannot exist. The proposed finite-case extension also evaluates f(1) when the finite domain is empty. Repair: require A nonempty for the surjection characterization, or state that A is empty or has a surjection from N. The injection-into-N characterization includes the empty case. The new introductory entry explicitly uses injections; it does not adopt the faulty equivalence.
